correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly splits the radical as a module over K tensor K, classifies all field-to-square-zero crossed derivations (zero for identity twist, inner for nonidentity), establishes both inclusions B intersect J = M using an explicit containing graph subalgebra, and identifies independent uniform rank matrices of r or r-1 rows. The full-generation formula follows by finite-field subfield Möbius inversion. Boundaries r=1, m=1, zero multiplicity and characteristic two are covered; standalone exhaustive algebra-closure tests over F4 reproduce six pair counts, two singleton counts and two conditional profile laws. Finite tests do not stand in for infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Against the inspected closest full-text work, the complete conditional joint rank distribution and all-tuple-length product formula are not stated or entailed as a formal specialization without additional analysis of crossed derivations and independent Galois-isotypic spans. Sercombe--Shalev (arXiv:2009.01115) prove global random-generation estimates and maximal-subalgebra class descriptions; Iovanov--Sistko (arXiv:1705.00762) classify maximal subalgebras structurally. The 2015 algebra-generator recursion is a general method, not an explicit twist-profile formula in the accessible material. Identical earlier formulations cannot be ruled out.
residual_risks: The general maximal-subalgebra machinery could make the factor law accessible to a specialist, even though an identical printed statement was not found.

value.rationale: This determines the full conditional isotypic radical-profile distribution, not a single isolated count, for every finite-dimensional local associative algebra with one finite-field residue and square-zero radical. It identifies the exact r versus r-1 generating-row deficit caused by each nontrivial Galois twist, gives all-r generation probabilities and sharp thresholds, and supports sampling and structural comparison of commutative and noncommutative local algebras. The invariant is directly motivated by the probability-of-generation question of Sercombe--Shalev; no downstream theorem is asserted.
